mirror_runs.both_satisfied: A supervisor build offers a named-agent picker on the reassign panel (R6 holds), while the ticket row ALSO carries three unlabelled icon buttons of which one reassigns; a support user reading the row cannot tell which moves the issue (R17 also holds). Naming the target inside the panel and leaving the row ambiguous are independent surfaces.
mirror_runs.both_unsatisfied: A build whose reassign action is a single clearly labelled 'Move to another agent' button that opens a free-text agent id field: nothing is ambiguous to the user (R17 does not hold), and the supervisor is never asked to pick the receiving agent by name from the roster (R6 does not hold).

mirror_runs.both_satisfied: A build renders the pinned light palette throughout (R11 holds) while labelling the detail panel fields 'assignee_id' and 'customer_id' in that same palette (R18 also holds). Colour fidelity and copy register are independent.
mirror_runs.both_unsatisfied: A build ships an unstyled default-framework grey theme that ignores the pinned palette (R11 does not hold) but labels every field in plain support language such as 'Assigned to' and 'Raised by' (R18 does not hold).

mirror_runs.both_satisfied: A build scopes the customer's own list correctly so that customer sees only issues they raised (R3 holds), while the agent navigation still exposes a reachable 'Reassign' route that an agent can open and submit from (R19 also holds). Read scoping on one screen and role affordance on another are independent surfaces.
mirror_runs.both_unsatisfied: A build leaks every customer's issues into one shared list (R3 does not hold) but exposes no supervisor-only action anywhere in the agent navigation (R19 does not hold).
